key_insight: UniAIR is a unified AI framework that can predict how mutations affect immune recognition across multiple settings, not just one task at a time. This makes mutation-effect prediction more generalizable across antibody, antigen, and T cell receptor interactions.
problem_solved: Existing models for mutation-effect prediction are often specialized for a single immune recognition context and do not transfer well across different adaptive immune systems. This paper addresses the need for a broader, unified model that works across diverse biological interaction types.
method: Develops a multimodal framework that integrates information from different immune recognition modalities.
Trains a single unified model to learn mutation-effect patterns across antibody, antigen, and TCR interactions.
Aims for cross-task generalization so predictions remain useful across diverse adaptive immune recognition settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how multimodal and unified modeling can improve transferability in complex biological prediction tasks. It also provides a template for building more generalizable models instead of maintaining separate systems for each subtype of interaction.

paper_title: Generalizable mutation-effect prediction across adaptive immune recognition via unified multimodal framework
paper_authors: Rong Han, Yumeng Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Lei Fu, Tong Pan
